tagline.text: Negros's oldest stone church and its 1879 bell tower

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0–300 (per person, local transport and snacks; check the entrance fee locally)

children.text: Dumaguete Cathedral is the cathedral parish of Saint Catherine of Alexandria, described as the oldest stone church on Negros Island. A detached bell tower built in 1879 stands beside the Baroque church completed in 1776, and Rizal Boulevard and Quezon Park are close by, which makes it ideal for a walking tour.

The official name of Dumaguete Cathedral is the Saint Catherine of Alexandria Cathedral Parish, and in Spanish it is Catedral Parroquial de Santa Catalina de Alejandria. It is a Roman Catholic church in the very center of Dumaguete, Negros Oriental, and the seat of the Diocese of Dumaguete. Wikipedia describes it as the oldest stone church on Negros Island. Even travelers just passing through Dumaguete can easily fit it into an itinerary, since it is within walking distance of the seafront promenade.

The parish dates back to 1620. It was founded when Dumaguete was a pueblo, and it is said to have originally covered southeastern Negros and even Siquijor. The stone church was begun in 1754 and completed in 1776, and between 1776 and 1855 the transept and an annex linking the church to the old convent were added. On November 25, 1846, a fire started by firecrackers during the town fiesta damaged the wooden ceiling, the altars, some pews and the organ, though the convent was spared. Afterward, in 1859–1866 Fr. Antonio Moreno added vestments and galvanized roofing, and in 1867–1879 Fr. Juan Felix de Encarnacion renovated the flooring. Until 1645 the early parish was served by eight secular priests, the first of whom was Fr. Juan de Roa y Herrera. Under Fr. Jose Fernandez de Septien, four watchtowers were built at the corners of the church lot to defend against raiders from the south, and today's bell tower stands on one of them. This story makes the church read as both a place of faith and a place with a history of defense.

In 1885 the portico was finished, and in 1886 two side altars were dedicated to the Virgen de Consolacion and Saint Joseph. The interior was painted, and in 1891 an organ made in Zaragoza was acquired. The Recollects left in 1898 during the Philippine Revolution and returned in 1909. When the Diocese of Dumaguete was founded in 1955, this church became its cathedral, and the current bishop of the diocese is Julito Cortes. The diocese was erected on April 5, 1955, by Pope Pius XII, and its first bishop was Epifanio Surban. It covers most of Negros Oriental and the province of Siquijor, with St. Catherine as patron and St. Joseph as secondary patron. In December 2024, nine papal awardees received their honors at this cathedral. Wikipedia also notes that renovations of key diocesan buildings, including the cathedral and the Bishop's Residence, took place under Bishop John Du (2001–2012).

The freestanding belfry beside the cathedral stands on an old watchtower. After restoration by the National Museum of the Philippines, the belfry was turned over to the Diocese of Dumaguete on 15 June 2026, and its Important Cultural Property marker was unveiled. Quezon Park and the National Museum’s Dumaguete branch are within walking distance.
This Baroque church was begun in 1754 and completed in 1776. Its look is simple and dignified, and traces of long years of additions and repairs remain in the building.
The separate belfry southeast of the cathedral was built on an old watchtower. Restoration and handover took place in 2026. Follow on-site instructions for the interior or stairs.

blocks.title: Prayer space under the bell tower

children.text: A grotto and a prayer area are at the foot of the bell tower. People may be praying quietly, so keep your voice low.
A monument to José Rizal stands in front of the cathedral. It is a good spot to fit the whole church and the monument into one frame.

blocks.title: Quezon Park and the National Museum branch

children.text: The cathedral, the bell tower and the National Museum branch (the Dumaguete Presidencia) are clustered near Quezon Park. A short walking loop within one district is possible.
The feast of St. Catherine is November 25. The 1846 fire also happened on this fiesta day, and the date remains a big event in Dumaguete.

St. Catherine's is the cathedral of the Diocese of Dumaguete, which covers most of Negros Oriental and Siquijor. For travelers, it is a place to see traditional religious events and town fiestas up close.

items.title: 1–2 hour walking route
items.subtitle: From the cathedral to the seafront promenade

children.text: Look around the José Rizal monument and the church facade in front of the cathedral. Check the diocese announcements for morning Mass times, and stay quiet during Mass.
See the 1879 bell tower to the southeast and the grotto below it. Notice the shape of the tower standing on an old watchtower.
Take a short walk toward nearby Quezon Park and the National Museum branch.
Walk to Rizal Boulevard and enjoy a coffee or snack while looking at the sea.
Check opening hours and museum operations locally.
Look around the cathedral and bell tower and take photos in the softer light as the sun sinks.
Walk to the waterfront and have a drink at a cafe along Rizal Boulevard.
Walk the Pantawan People's Park promenade from the port to the mouth of the Banica River and try the snacks from the street stalls.
Street stall menus and hours can differ from day to day.
There are daily flights from Manila to Dumaguete-Sibulan Airport (DGT), reportedly operated by Cebu Pacific, Cebgo and PAL Express. The airport is in Sibulan, north of the city.
Airlines and schedules change often, so check before you book.

items.title: From Manila by ferry or bus

children.text: 2GO Travel ferries are described as linking Manila and Dumaguete.
By land, Ceres buses are known to run from the Calindagan terminal to Cebu City and to Cubao, Metro Manila.

items.title: By ferry from Cebu, Bohol and Siquijor

children.text: From the Port of Dumaguete there are regular ferries to Cebu, Bohol, Mindanao and Siquijor. Operators include FastCat, Aleson Shipping Lines, Montenegro Lines and Ocean Jet.
The main transport in Dumaguete is the tricycle, which is described as carrying up to six passengers. The area around the cathedral is a walkable distance.
For destinations outside the city, use jeepneys or buses.

Dumaguete has a tropical monsoon climate, with a rainy season from June to November and a dry season from December to May. April and May are the hottest months. The 1991–2020 averages are a maximum of about

From late October to early March the northeast monsoon (amihan) is said to bring relatively cool, dry conditions. The area around the cathedral is a walking route, so morning or evening is more comfortable than midday.

Around November 25, the feast of St. Catherine, the cathedral and downtown get crowded and events take place. You can enjoy a lively atmosphere if you time your visit to the fiesta, but it is better to book accommodation in advance.

Rizal Boulevard, lined with hotels, cafes, restaurants and bars, is close to the cathedral. Wikipedia explains that many of its businesses were converted from old sugar mansions and ancestral houses, and says you can enjoy views of Dumaguete Bay and the islands of Cebu and Siquijor beyond it.

Along the seaside Pantawan People's Park promenade there are stalls selling balut, tempura, kikiam and fishballs. After seeing the cathedral and bell tower, it is a good route for a light bite while continuing on foot.

Silliman University, close to the cathedral, was founded in 1901 and its campus of about 610,000 square meters adjoins downtown. Landmarks include Silliman Hall, Hibbard Hall (home of the Anthropology Museum), Katipunan Hall, Luce Auditorium and the library. Ferries run from the Port of Dumaguete to Siquijor, Cebu and Bohol, so it is also easy to follow the cathedral with a trip to a neighboring island.
The cathedral is a place of prayer for worshippers, so modest clothing suits it better than shorts or sleeveless tops.
During Mass, refrain from taking photos and making loud noise, and check the schedule through the diocese announcements.
Going early in the morning or in the late afternoon as the sun lowers means less glare and softer photos.
If you walk the cathedral, bell tower, Quezon Park, the National Museum branch and Rizal Boulevard in one go, half a day is enough.
Around the November 25 feast of St. Catherine the city is crowded, so book accommodation and transport in advance.
Check parish guidance and posted signs for access to the belfry interior and stairs.
Walking from nearby Silliman University to Rizal Boulevard lets you see downtown Dumaguete in half a day.
Have lunch near the cathedral and plan the day to end with sunset along the Pantawan People's Park promenade, and it flows naturally.
Turn off your phone sound inside and around the church so you do not disturb worshippers' prayers, and be careful not to catch people's faces when you take photos.
The cathedral is a place where worship actually takes place, so avoid behavior that disturbs people during Mass.
Mass and event times and the areas open to visitors can change, so follow local guidance and diocese announcements.
Respect access signs and any barriers protecting the belfry.
The midday sun is strong in the hot season, so bring water and a hat.
In the rainy season, check for sudden rain and typhoon news.
Flight and ferry schedules change often, so check with the operator before you leave.
A seafront promenade within walking distance of the cathedral, with hotels, cafes, restaurants and bars and views of Dumaguete Bay and the islands toward Cebu and Siquijor.
A campus founded in 1901 that adjoins downtown, with Hibbard Hall, home of the Anthropology Museum.
See the whole city around the cathedral, including itineraries, accommodation, the port and transport.
A neighboring island reached by regular ferries from the Port of Dumaguete.
